challenge.method: SCES-1.0 §§2–4 and Protocol stage 7 require fresh inspection of the exact revision, six checks per binding, preservation of conditions, and a targeted challenge to an identity merge. I examined all 23 contiguous parts and tested whether a document’s copying notice, a component attribution, or a newer texinfo.tex could serve as the witness.
challenge.results: The @copying and @insertcopying definitions in part 15 store and reproduce text supplied by the document. The attribution in part 20 concerns UTF-8 code adapted from LaTeX. Neither states the TeX processing exception. The header itself warns that distributed copies can differ from the latest version. The decisive witness is the inline notice in the pinned specimen.

limitations: The notice governs the identified macro file and gives permission concerning the result under the stated condition. The source document, incorporated material, other project files, and products of unrelated TeX runs require their own licensing evidence.

The inspection used the commit-pinned Automake mirror. SPDX supplies the GNU Savannah release-specific citation. A separate comparison against a GNU release archive was outside the inspected evidence.

The adopted bundle SHA-256 14da3f31f697ab828d4a4560f060dbe511861020db54bea7bc531e20ea0855ce is the supplied policy pin. reasoning: The GNU Texinfo macro file identifies itself as texinfo.tex version 2021-04-25.21 and names Free Software Foundation, Inc. as copyright holder. Its inline header, lines 23–26, says that when TeX reads this file while processing a Texinfo source document, “you may use the result without restriction.” The next sentence expressly designates the exception as an additional permission under section 7 of GPL version 3. This supports the License Index mapping to an active exception named “Texinfo exception.” The name and active state are editorial registry fields.
